robot-dance.context: A dancer with a square head, arms bent at sharp right angles and stiff straight legs, with short ticks beside the elbows. Used for robot and popping dance, street dance classes and mechanical movement.

highland-fling.context: A dancer in a pleated kilt balanced on one foot with the other foot tucked at the knee and both arms curved overhead. Used for Scottish highland dance, folk dance events and Celtic festivals.

vogue-dance.context: A dancer framing the face with both hands in sharp angular poses with one hip pushed out. Used for voguing, ballroom scene, runway style dance and pose battles.

twist-dance.context: A dancer with bent knees turned to one side and arms swinging the other way, with a curved twist line at the hips. Used for twist dance, retro party themes and sixties music events.

pole-dance.context: A dancer holding a vertical pole with one hand and hooking one knee around it while leaning out. Used for pole dance and pole fitness classes, studios and acrobatic dance.

bhangra-dance.context: A dancer in a loose tunic with both arms raised high and one knee lifted. Used for bhangra, Punjabi folk dance, harvest festivals and South Asian celebrations.

samba-dancer.context: A dancer with a huge semicircular fan of feathers behind the whole body and one hip cocked. Used for samba, carnival parades, Brazilian events and feathered costumes.

folklorico-dance.context: A dancer holding a very wide ruffled skirt out to both sides with a flower in the hair. Used for ballet folklorico, Mexican folk dance, Latin heritage events and cultural festivals.

fire-knife-dance.context: A short staff with flames at both ends held in a hand, with curved motion lines on either side. Used for fire knife dancing, Polynesian shows, fire spinning and luau entertainment.

roller-disco.context: A skater gliding on quad roller skates with one arm pointing up towards a small disco ball. Used for roller disco nights, retro rink parties and skate dance events.

hopak-dance.context: A dancer in a deep squat with arms folded across the chest kicking one leg straight out. Used for the hopak and Cossack squat dance, Ukrainian folk performance and kicking dance moves.

tap-dancer.context: A dancer in a bowler hat holding a short cane out while one heel is kicked up, with small tap marks by the shoe. Used for tap dance, musical theatre and vaudeville style shows.

aerial-silks.context: A performer hanging upside down between two long fabric strips that fall from a single rigging point, legs split. Used for aerial silks, aerial fabric classes and circus performance.

teeterboard.context: A seesaw board on a low fulcrum with one acrobat standing on the raised end and another flying tucked in the air above. Used for teeterboard, Korean plank and catapult acrobatics in circus acts.

rola-bola.context: A performer standing on a flat board that rests on a horizontal cylinder with arms out to the sides for balance. Used for rola bola and balance board acts in circus and street shows.

human-cannonball.context: A wheeled cannon pointing upward with a performer shooting out of the muzzle in a straight line. Used for the human cannonball act, daredevil stunts and circus shows.

fire-juggling.context: Three flaming torches fanning up out of two open cupped hands. Used for fire juggling, fire shows, circus acts and street performance.

clown-shoes.context: A pair of oversized clown shoes with long soles and big round toes. Used for clown costumes, circus themes, comedy and party outfits.

squirting-flower.context: A flower pinned to a jacket lapel squirting a thin arc of water drops. Used for the classic clown gag, pranks, joke shops and slapstick comedy.

circus-pedestal.context: A short drum-shaped stand with a star on the side and a scalloped top rim. Used for circus animal acts, lion taming scenes and big top decorations.

circus-wagon.context: An ornate circus cage wagon with vertical bars, a scalloped roof edge and two large wheels. Used for traveling circus themes, menagerie scenes and old-time carnival graphics.

bed-of-nails.context: A performer lying flat on a board covered with rows of upright spikes. Used for fakir acts, sideshow stunts and demonstrations of pressure and pain tolerance.

escape-artist.context: A standing figure wrapped in crossing chains with a padlock on the chest. Used for escape acts, classic escape stunts, magic shows and bondage escape challenges.

levitation-illusion.context: A figure lying horizontally in mid air above a low table with a hoop passing around the body. Used for levitation magic tricks, floating illusions and stage magic shows.

hypnosis-pendulum.context: A pocket watch with a spiral on its face swinging from a chain between two curved swing lines. Used for hypnosis, hypnotherapy, trance and mesmerizing effects.

mentalist.context: A face with fingertips pressed to both temples and short rays shooting out from the forehead. Used for mentalism, mind reading acts, psychic shows and concentration.

magic-cabinet.context: An upright cabinet on short legs with a star on one door and a crescent moon on the other. Used for vanishing cabinet tricks, magician props and stage illusion shows.

vanishing-act.context: A standing figure dissolving into scattered dots on one side with a small puff of smoke at the feet. Used for disappearing tricks, magic shows and anything that fades or vanishes.

rising-rope-trick.context: A rope curling straight up out of a woven basket, with a small figure climbing it. Used for the Indian rope trick, snake charmer scenes and classic street magic.

spoon-bending.context: A spoon with its handle bent over at a sharp angle and curved lines around the bend. Used for spoon bending, psychokinesis, mentalism and telekinesis demonstrations.

pie-in-face.context: A round face with a cream pie pressed flat across it and drips of cream running down. Used for slapstick comedy, pranks, food fights and custard pie gags.

disguise-glasses.context: Novelty glasses with an attached big nose, bushy eyebrows and a thick moustache. Used for disguises, joke shops, fancy dress and undercover or incognito themes.

spring-eye-glasses.context: Novelty glasses with two eyeballs bouncing out of the lenses on coiled springs. Used for googly eyes, surprise reactions, joke shops and party costumes.

spring-punch-glove.context: A boxing glove shooting out of a small box on a zigzag spring. Used for jack in the box style pranks, surprise gags, punching toys and joke gifts.

jester-marotte.context: A short stick topped with a carved jester head wearing a three-pointed hat with bells. Used for court jester props, medieval fools, comedy and carnival costumes.

zanni-mask.context: A half mask with arched brows and a very long pointed nose, as worn in commedia dell'arte. Used for Italian comedy, theatre history, carnival and mask-making.

rimshot.context: A snare drum and a crash cymbal on a stand with a drumstick striking the rim and small hit marks. Used for punchline jokes, ba dum tss reactions and stand-up comedy.

chattering-teeth.context: A wind-up set of big grinning false teeth on little feet with a key on the side. Used for wind-up toys, joke shop novelties and novelty teeth gags.

arrow-through-head.context: A smiling head with a novelty arrow whose front and back halves stick out either side. Used for the classic arrow headband gag, silly costumes and joke props.

stage-door.context: A plain door with a star above it, the entrance backstage for performers. Used for stage door entrances, backstage access and the performer entry of a theatre.

theater-seat.context: A padded auditorium seat with a rounded back, armrests and a small number plate. Used for theatre seat booking, cinema seats, row and seat numbers and venue maps.

play-script.context: A bound script page with brass fasteners showing a character name above each block of dialogue. Used for play scripts, screenplays, rehearsals and learning lines.

stage-flying.context: A performer in a harness hanging from two wires beneath a rail above the stage floor. Used for stage flying effects, aerial rigging and theatre stunts.

zig-zag-illusion.context: A tall cabinet in three sections with the middle one shifted sideways and a face in the top window. Used for the zig zag girl illusion, stage magic and cabinet tricks.

sword-basket-illusion.context: A wicker basket pierced by two crossed swords at different angles. Used for sword basket magic tricks, stage illusions and fakir acts.

harlequin-costume.context: A figure in a diamond-patterned suit with a wide bicorne hat. Used for Harlequin costumes, commedia dell'arte, carnival dress and pantomime.
